metadata.title: Claude, Contact Research.
metadata.purpose: Answer whether Claude already knows a specific person, or has to go find out, using the contact-research skill's own trigger-phrase and pipeline rule as the concrete case. Lands the carry-out that the skill doesn't make Claude know a person -- it makes Claude look them up, in the same steps, only when the words match its triggers.
metadata.anchor_pair: B02 -> B03 ('who is Jane Doe at Acme' run through the same three-step pipeline, then run again unchanged; contrasted with a non-matching request that never starts it)

beats.narration_text: You ask Claude about a specific person, and it feels like it should already know everything about them. It doesn't -- it has to go look them up first. So how does that lookup actually work?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'You ask about a person. Claude must already know, right?', hesitates on 'know', corrects to 'look them up'

props.text:

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('know' -> 'look them up') is visible on a late frame.

beats.narration_text: It's a reasonable guess -- Claude does hold a lot of general knowledge about people. But whether someone's a warm lead right now depends on today's signals: a recent reply, a meeting booked, a title change. None of that lives in anything Claude was trained on. Answering from memory alone would mean guessing, not researching.

shot.new_visual_element: A frozen 'trained on' date on a calendar; three signal cards -- reply received, meeting booked, title change -- arriving after it, out of reach

production_viz.label: Today's signals aren't in memory
production_viz.mechanic: A calendar card on the left is stamped 'TRAINED ON' with a fixed date, then freezes -- no further marks land on it. To the right, three small cards draw in one at a time along a timeline running past that frozen date: 'reply received', 'meeting booked', 'title change', each stamped with today's date. A dotted line from the frozen calendar toward the three cards fails to reach them and fades.

beats.narration_text: The fix is contact-research, a SKILL.md file Claude reads before it acts -- instructions, not memory. It only fires when your words match its triggers: 'who is this person,' 'is this person a warm lead,' phrases like that. Say 'who is Jane Doe at Acme,' and it runs the same three steps every time: read the file, pull the contact's Common Room signals, return them.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR -- 'who is Jane Doe at Acme' matched against the trigger list, then walked through Read, Execute, Return

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR -- matched, then walked step by step
production_viz.mechanic: A SKILL.md card sits at top with a short list of trigger phrases beneath it: 'who is [name]', 'is [name] a warm lead'. THE ANCHOR. The words 'who is Jane Doe at Acme' type themselves out below, a bracket snaps to the matching trigger phrase, and the query flows left to right through three labelled stations -- READ, EXECUTE, RETURN -- lighting each in turn. THIS EXACT SEQUENCE RETURNS AT B03.

beats.narration_text: Run 'who is Jane Doe at Acme' again next month, and Claude walks the same three steps -- that's what a written spec buys you: repeatable, not remembered. But phrase it outside the trigger list, some open-ended question about a person the file never anticipated, and the pipeline never starts. You're back to Claude answering from what it already knows -- the exact guess we started with.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS -- the same query run again, identical steps; then a non-matching question that never enters the pipeline

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS -- same steps again, then nothing starts
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 SEQUENCE RETURNS, identical: 'who is Jane Doe at Acme' flows through READ, EXECUTE, RETURN again, same lighted path. Beside it, a different, unmatched question types itself out, no bracket snaps to any trigger, and the three stations stay dark -- the query simply sits there, going nowhere. A line of small italic text appears beneath: 'no match. no pipeline. just Claude, on its own.'

beats.narration_text: contact-research doesn't make Claude know a person. It makes Claude look them up, the same way every time -- only when your words match what it was built to hear.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt -- read it with me. I want to research a specific person using Common Room data. Read the contact-research skill and walk me through what you'll do, step by step, before you do it. Watch for two things: does Claude name the exact trigger phrase your words matched, and does it lay out the steps before running them? Liam, in for Bear.
